items.followUp: Define phishing and briefly explain identity theft.

rubric.why: Credit the definition of cyber crime as illegal activity involving computers or the internet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cyber crime is an illegal activity carried out using a computer or the internet.

rubric.why: Advance fee fraud involves asking the victim to pay money in advance.
rubric.description: Identifies the advance fee paid by the victim.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning an upfront or advance fee/payment.

rubric.why: The advance payment is requested in return for a promised reward, prize, or benefit.
rubric.description: Explains the promised reward or benefit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the victim is promised a reward, prize, or other benefit.

rubric.why: Hacking involves accessing a computer or network without authorization.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that hacking is unauthorized access to a computer or network.

modelAnswer: Cyber crime is illegal activity carried out using computers or the internet.
In advance fee fraud, a criminal asks a victim to pay an upfront fee in return for a promised reward, prize, or benefit.
Hacking is gaining unauthorized access to a computer or network, often to view, steal, or change information.

items.followUp: Write an algorithm for brushing your teeth.

rubric.why: Socks must be put on before shoes.
rubric.description: Places socks before shoes in the sequence.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing that socks are worn before shoes.

rubric.why: A clear algorithm should include the essential actions and a beginning and end.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a sequence that puts socks and shoes on both feet and has start and stop steps.

modelAnswer: Put on the left sock, then the right sock.
Put on the left shoe, then the right shoe.

items.followUp: Write down any two advantages of using a flowchart.

rubric.why: A flowchart presents the steps of a process visually.
rubric.description: States that a flowchart is a graphical or visual representation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct property of a flowchart.

rubric.why: Flowcharts use standard symbols and directional arrows and can make a process easier to understand or communicate.
rubric.description: States another correct property of a flowchart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second correct, distinct property.

modelAnswer: A flowchart is a graphical representation of an algorithm or process.
It uses standard symbols and arrows to show the sequence and direction of steps.

items.followUp: Write down one difference between a program and an algorithm.

rubric.why: An algorithm is expressed as a step-by-step procedure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying an algorithm as a sequence of steps or instructions.

rubric.why: A flowchart represents steps visually using symbols and arrows.
rubric.description: Describes a flowchart in contrast to an algorithm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a flowchart as a graphical or symbol-based representation.

modelAnswer: An algorithm is a step-by-step written procedure for solving a problem.
A flowchart is a graphical representation of the procedure using standard symbols and arrows.

items.followUp: Convert (101101)₂ into the decimal number system.

rubric.why: Correctly assigns powers of 2 to the binary digits and evaluates the place values.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct expansion or equivalent place-value calculation.
Award 1 mark for the correct answer, 23.

items.followUp: Write down any two input devices.

rubric.why: A hard disk, USB/flash drive, memory card, optical disc, floppy disk, or SSD is a storage device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid storage device.

rubric.why: A second distinct valid example is required for full credit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for another valid storage device, distinct from the first.

items.followUp: Draw the truth table for the AND operator.

rubric.why: The truth table should identify its inputs and the OR operation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for clearly identifying the two input variables and the OR operator.

rubric.why: These are the four correct input-output rows for the OR operator.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for all four correct rows, including the output for each input pair.

rubric.why: A compound proposition is made from two or more simple propositions.
rubric.description: States that it combines simple propositions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a compound proposition combines at least two simple propositions.

rubric.why: Logical connectives such as AND, OR, and NOT are used to combine propositions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning a logical connective or giving a correct example.

modelAnswer: A compound proposition is a proposition formed by combining two or more simple propositions.
The propositions are joined using logical connectives such as AND, OR, or NOT.
